OpenAssistant messages: a dated, multilingual example corpus

Source: R/data.R
oasst_messages.Rd

1,485 messages from OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST2): every eligible message that carries an emoji (750) and as many emoji-free ones (735), written between 2023-01-17 and 2023-10-30 in 17 languages, by people asking ("prompter", 508) and by people writing the assistant's replies ("assistant", 977). It is the example data of the vignettes and help pages since 0.7.0, and the reaction tallies on the same messages are in oasst_reactions.

Usage

oasst_messages

Format

A tibble with 1,485 rows and 6 columns:

message_id

OASST2's identifier for the message.

parent_id

The message this one replies to, so replies can be told from opening prompts (117 have NA). The parent need not be in the sample: 1,315 rows reply to a message that is not.

created_at

When the message was written, a POSIXct in UTC.

role

"prompter" or "assistant". Both are written by people; OASST2's model-written messages are excluded with the synthetic ones.

lang

The language OASST2 records, as a BCP 47 tag ("en", "pt-BR").

text

The message as written, line breaks included.

Source

Kopf A, Kilcher Y, von Rutte D, Anagnostidis S, Tam ZR, Stevens K, et al. (2023). OpenAssistant Conversations: Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment. NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07327. Data from https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenAssistant/oasst2, file 2023-11-05_oasst2_ready.messages.jsonl.gz at revision 179dd21fc55192153d94adb0e0ce8f69e222bf75, released under the Apache License 2.0, whose text inst/LICENSE.note reproduces. Processed by data-raw/oasst.R, which rebuilds the sample offline from a committed extract of the eligible messages.

Details

Emoji are rare in real text, so the sample is stratified on them: about half the rows carry one, where 1.03% of all OASST2 messages do. Figures computed on it describe this sample, not OASST2, and not chat in general.

How the sample was drawn

From the 135,174 messages of the "ready" release, in this order: messages marked deleted (4,376) and synthetic (0) were dropped; then those whose largest detoxify score is 0.1 or more (2,092); those matching a word-list screen for slurs (23); those holding an e-mail address, a phone-number shape or a URL with a query string (1,021); and those longer than 600 code points (36,614), so printed examples stay readable. That left 91,048 messages, 751 of them carrying an emoji.

The toxicity scores and the word list are English-centred, and 107 of the 751 emoji-bearing messages had no detoxify score at all (Portuguese, Chinese, German, Japanese and Ukrainian among them). Each of those was read in full before the data was committed, as was every row an example or a vignette prints, and a message was to be removed if it was sexual, hateful or harassing or held personal data the automatic screens missed: one was, for describing the sexual abuse of minors. data-raw/oasst-read-out.csv lists it with its rule.

The sample is every remaining emoji-bearing message and an equal number of emoji-free ones, allocated across month by role by language in proportion to the emoji-free messages and drawn with set.seed(20261106). "Carries an emoji" is the package's own detection when the extract was built.

See also

oasst_reactions for the tallies; emoji_trend() and emoji_from_counts() for the verbs that need what the old example corpus lacked, a date and a tally.

Examples

emoji_summary(oasst_messages, text)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   n_with_emoji n_total n_orphan_components n_invalid_flags n_hidden
#>          <int>   <int>               <int>           <int>    <int>
#> 1          750    1485                   0               0        0
table(oasst_messages$role)
#> 
#> assistant  prompter 
#>       977       508
